title: Blog Format Showcase — All Components
excerpt: A living style reference for every formatting element available in the blog: headings, callouts, tables, blockquotes, images, and more.
body: This post demonstrates every available formatting component — a reference for future writing. The blog supports HTML within JSON body arrays, rendered into .article-body with magazine-style typography.
Three levels of sub-headings are available below the post title.
H3 has a thin teal left border and uses the system UI font. It's good for breaking down sections within an H2.
H4 is italic, uses a lighter colour and a subtle left border. Useful for minor asides or nested details. Try not to go deeper than H4 — if you need H5, the section probably needs restructuring.

Standard paragraphs use Noto Serif SC, a reading-optimised serif stack. Bold text renders slightly darker than body, and italics use the same serif face in italic weight. Inline code is set in Fira Code at ~82% size with accent colour. Links are underlined in accent colour.

Blockquotes are styled as centred pull quotes with decorative open-quote marks and accent-coloured top/bottom borders:
Research is mostly failure dressed up as iteration. The paper is just the part where things finally work.
They work best for a single impactful sentence — a takeaway or a moment of reflection.
Three callout variants provide sidebar-style emphasis boxes:

Default Callout
Uses the accent-2 (teal) left border. Best for core insights, definitions, or key takeaways that should not be missed.

Info Callout
Blue left border. Use for background context, related work, or supplementary information that supports but isn't central to the main argument.

Warning Callout
Amber left border. Use for caveats, lessons learned from failure, experimental pitfalls, or anything the reader should approach with caution.
Tables use a minimal, industrial style with uppercase header labels:
By default, all images in the article body are positioned in the right gutter, vertically centred on their <img> tag location. The text column stays image-free — no wrapping, no overlap.
Place an <img> tag at the point in the text where you want the thumbnail to appear:

When two images are placed close together (anchor gap <220px), they automatically split — one to the right gutter, the next to the left gutter. This prevents overlap and creates a balanced magazine spread:
The second image will appear on the left side because its anchor is close to the previous one. With sufficient spacing between images, the side resets to right.
For figures that need to stay in the text column, use class='img-x' — the image renders at 60% column width, centred:
Horizontal rules are rendered as a centred section symbol (§) instead of a line — a typographic touch that suits the magazine aesthetic.
That covers all available formats. When writing new posts, copy this structure and adapt.
